clue.text: Something one may have to bear, like this clue

definitions.text: Something one may have to bear
definitions.meaning: a burden or trial carried through life, as in 'we all have a cross to bear'
this clue sits in the horizontal set of the grid

explanation.surface: A grumbling solver complains that this clue is a burden to be endured.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the answer is a burden one bears, and as one word it names the direction of this very clue.

clue.text: What a youth got from glancing at a flapper's legs?

definitions.text: What a youth got from glancing at a flapper's legs?

parts.words: What a youth got from glancing at a flapper's legs?
parts.note: a flapper's short skirts showed the lower legs, so a boy's first crush would come from the backs of her shins

explanation.surface: A 1920s boy is smitten on seeing a young woman's legs below her short skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A flapper was a fashionable 1920s young woman in short skirts; the fleshy back of the lower leg gives the first half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the phrase for a short-lived adolescent infatuation, the kind a youth develops.

clue.text: Excessive amount caught check-up needed

parts.note: over means too much, excessive
a haul is the amount of fish caught

explanation.surface: Too big a catch means the boat needs inspecting.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough examination and repair of machinery is a full inspection, a check-up.

clue.text: Get right celebrity on panel

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a board is a panel of people, or a flat panel of wood

explanation.surface: A famous person is invited to join an interview panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is the side of a ship as one faces forward.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or aircraft this nautical term means the right-hand side facing forward.

clue.text: Vessel seen crossing the harbour bar?

definitions.text: Vessel seen crossing the harbour bar?

parts.words: Vessel seen crossing the harbour bar?
parts.note: reads as a sailing ship passing over the sandbank at a harbour mouth, but also as a tall beer glass carried across a pub counter

explanation.surface: A sailing ship clears the sandbar at the mouth of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'harbour bar' is a sandbank, but a bar is also where drinks are served, and this word is also a large sherry or beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and a large drinking glass, both vessels.

clue.text: Trifle on top of tinned meat? That's nothing at all!

indicators.note: on top of means the pudding comes above the meat in this down answer

parts.note: a trifle is a sweet, a pudding of sponge, custard and cream
Fanny Adams was Royal Navy slang for tinned mutton, after a notorious 1867 murder

explanation.surface: A diner served trifle on tinned meat complains the meal is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered pudding; 'sweet' is the British word for dessert. The answer is a British euphemism for 'nothing at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang expression means absolutely nothing, a polite stand-in for a ruder phrase.

clue.text: A Manx cat having lost one of its nine lives?

definitions.text: A Manx cat having lost one of its nine lives?

parts.words: A Manx cat having lost one of its nine lives?
parts.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so 'puss' loses an S; and with one life gone only eight remain, giving octo- in front

explanation.surface: A tailless cat from the Isle of Man has used up one of its lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats have no tail, so PUSS is docked to PUS; nine lives less one is eight, OCTO. The eight-armed sea creature results.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea creature with eight arms is fancifully an eight-lived cat with its tail missing.

clue.text: Tchaikovsky found it in cracker

parts.note: Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker, and what a nutcracker opens is a hazelnut, called by its French name

explanation.surface: The composer discovers something inside a festive cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' suggests a Christmas cracker, but it means a nutcracker; the answer is French for a hazelnut, and also a small round of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word means hazelnut, the kind of thing a nutcracker breaks open.

clue.text: Quiet, flushed, about to treat

indicators.note: about says the flushed word goes around the treating word

parts.note: flushed means red in the face
to serve someone is to treat them, as in served them badly

explanation.surface: A shy person blushed when about to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shy and reticent keeps their feelings to themselves, a quiet sort of person.

clue.text: Foreign crew said to put one off

parts.note: alien means foreign, from another country

indicators.note: said signals that the word for the crew is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a rowing crew is an eight

explanation.surface: A rowing crew from overseas is described as off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing boat's crew is an 'eight'; spoken, it gives ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to turn them away or make them unfriendly, so it puts a person off.

clue.text: Old militant ladies protect family soldier's name

indicators.note: protect means the women's service wraps around the family word, guarding it

parts.note: the ATS, Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British women's army branch in the Second World War
kin means family

explanation.surface: Wartime women soldiers shield a relative while reciting a soldier's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Atkins was the specimen name on British army forms, so the surname became the generic private's name.

clue.text: A wager — a literal arrangement

parts.note: the letter A is alpha in Greek and in the radio code
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet and then sets out some letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' here means made of letters, not 'exact'.
explanation.definitionFit: The set of letters in their fixed order is an arrangement of letters, which is what 'literal' means here.

clue.text: Seem to act as counsel

definitions.meaning: to look or give the impression of being
a barrister is said to come into court for a client, representing them

explanation.surface: A lawyer merely looks as if they are representing a client.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both look or seem, and turn up in court on behalf of a party as their barrister.

clue.text: Girl has things to sell, quite unexpectedly

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
wares are goods offered for sale

explanation.surface: A young woman turns out, surprisingly, to have goods for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught off guard is to be taken by surprise, so it happens without warning.

clue.text: With a girl, chatter about love — and disappear

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: about says the chatter word goes around the love letter

parts.note: prate means idle chatter
love is zero in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A man talks about love to a young woman, then vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid turning to vapour vanishes from sight, so the verb is used for anything that fades away.

clue.text: Terrible mountain

definitions.meaning: an old and poetic adjective meaning fierce, cruel or deadly
a hill or high moorland, especially in the north of England

explanation.surface: A frightening peak looms ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic adjective for cruel or deadly, and a northern English noun for a hill or moor.

clue.text: Lost courage, but led after smash

indicators.note: smash means the letters of these words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone lost their nerve after following a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash' looks like a crash that followed; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver or hesitate is to lose nerve, a synonym for losing courage.

clue.text: A more permanent bit of the fuselage?

definitions.text: A more permanent bit of the fuselage?

parts.words: A more permanent bit of the fuselage?
parts.note: split into two words this aircraft spar reads as something that stays attached for a greater time

explanation.surface: An engineer asks which part of an aircraft body lasts longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a lengthwise strut in an aircraft body; split in two it reads 'longer on', which is what 'more permanent' plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a main longitudinal member of an aircraft fuselage, a structural part of it.

clue.text: Was duty-bound to accept direction to lead

indicators.note: to accept means the obligation word takes the compass letter inside it

parts.note: had, as in 'had to', means was obliged
E is the abbreviation for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone felt obliged to take directions in order to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at the front or in charge of something is to guide it, a synonym of lead.

clue.text: College dinner one has a way to tackle

parts.note: in Oxford and Cambridge colleges, hall is the formal evening meal
the Roman numeral I is one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A student has found a route to tackle the formal college dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a ship's ropes; this rope hoists a sail or flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope used to hoist a sail is part of a ship's rigging, which sailors call tackle.

clue.text: A quiet river place is to the purpose

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
the Po is a river in northern Italy
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A calm riverside spot is said to be fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relevant or apt suits the matter in hand, which the old phrase calls to the purpose.

clue.text: It's good-bye to the garden for ant-eaters and such

indicators.note: to here means joined on after, the farewell attached to the garden

parts.note: the Garden of Eden in Genesis
ta-ta is an informal British farewell

explanation.surface: Animals that eat insects bid farewell to paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological order of toothless mammals, including sloths and armadillos as well as anteaters.

clue.text: The chucker-out gave order to cover it

indicators.note: gave order to means these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A bouncer was told to keep it under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave order to' looks like a command issued; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns tenants out of a property is someone who throws people out, a chucker-out.

clue.text: When it gets hot, this river can be fierce

indicators.note: when it gets says the river name, once a letter is added, becomes the fierce word; so the river is that word less the letter

parts.note: tigrish means fierce like a tiger
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A river in the heat turns ferocious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: add H (hot) to the river's name and you get TIGRISH, tiger-like and fierce.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of Mesopotamia flows through Turkey and Iraq; 'this river' points at the answer itself.

clue.text: Ahead over there — the Devil!

parts.note: read as 'a head': poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax per head
yon means over there, as in yonder

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a warning about Satan up ahead in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' must be split as 'a head', A + POLL. The answer is the destroying angel of Revelation and the fiend in Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon is the Greek name of the angel of the bottomless pit, used by Bunyan for Satan, a name for the Devil.

clue.text: Alas! for the — of Christian charity" (Hood)

definitions.text: Alas! for the — of Christian charity" (Hood)

parts.words: Alas! for the — of Christian charity" (Hood)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Thomas Hood's poem The Bridge of Sighs, about a drowned woman

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse laments how scarce kindness is.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood's lines run 'Alas! for the ___ / Of Christian charity / Under the sun!'; the missing word means scarcity and rhymes with charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means scarceness, which is Hood's complaint about Christian kindness.

clue.text: Yarns with foundation in an up-country march

parts.note: an ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
a basis is a foundation

explanation.surface: Tall tales are found to have some grounding in a long trek inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarns' are stories here, not wool. Xenophon's book of this name tells of a Greek army's march inland into Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word means a going-up, used for a military expedition from the coast into the interior.

clue.text: Change is under a penny

indicators.note: change means the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their coins add up to less than a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like loose coins; it is the anagram signal. The old British abbreviation d for a penny came from this Roman coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman silver coin is rendered 'penny' in the King James Bible and gave its initial to the pre-decimal penny.

clue.text: Supplied directly in death

indicators.note: in places the directly word inside the death word

parts.note: end means death, the end of life
due means directly or exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A deathbed bequest was made straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: To be invested or provided with a quality is to be furnished with it, so the word means supplied.
